nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management)

medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and titrate up to 5 mg daily if tolerated
medications.purpose: Reduce proteinuria and slow CKD progression; control hypertension
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first‑line treatment: ACE inhibitor or ARB for CKD with proteinuria or hypertension; monitor creatinine and potassium after 1‑2 weeks

medications.duration: Lifelong — lipid profile review at 12 weeks, then annually
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction in CKD and established IHD
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first‑line treatment: Statin for all CKD patients as a cardiovascular risk equivalent

medications.duration: Until 25‑OH vitamin D >30 ng/mL, then review annually
medications.purpose: Correct vitamin D deficiency and manage CKD‑MBD
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends vitamin D supplementation after confirming deficiency in CKD‑MBD

medications.duration: 4 weeks then reassess Hb, ferritin and TSAT; continue if still deficient
medications.purpose: Treat iron‑deficiency anemia of chronic kidney disease
medications.nice_justification: NG203 advises anemia screening and iron replacement when ferritin <100 µg/L or TSAT <20%

contraindications.reason: eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² – risk of lactic acidosis (NG203 contraindicated drug list)
eGFR 6 mL/min/1.73 m² is below the approved threshold of ≥20 mL/min/1.73 m² (NG203/TA775)
Accelerate CKD progression and cause fluid retention; contraindicated in CKD stage 4 (NG203)
Increases risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury; NG203 contraindicates dual RAAS blockade
contraindications.alternative: Use either ACE‑I or ARB, not both

contraindications.reason: Nephrotoxic and requires dose adjustment; contraindicated in eGFR <30 (NG203)
High risk of contrast‑induced nephropathy with eGFR <30 (NG203)
contraindications.alternative: Use low‑osmolar contrast with prophylactic hydration if imaging unavoidable

assumptions_warnings: Baseline serum potassium, sodium, bicarbonate, calcium, phosphate, PTH, 25‑OH vitamin D, ferritin, TSAT, and Hb are not available – these labs must be obtained before initiating ACE‑I, vitamin D, and iron therapy.
Liver function tests are not documented – required before starting atorvastatin.
Allergy status (ACE‑I cough, statin myopathy) is unknown – verify with patient before prescribing.
Blood pressure reading not provided – assume hypertension uncontrolled; monitor BP after starting ramipril and adjust as needed.
QRISK score not calculated – CKD and IHD already make patient high risk, but formal QRISK assessment is recommended for statin intensity decisions.
treatment_summary: Start ramipril 1.25 mg daily and atorvastatin 20 mg nightly as first‑line therapies per NICE NG203 to slow CKD progression, reduce proteinuria, and lower cardiovascular risk. Add cholecalciferol 800 IU daily and ferrous sulphate 200 mg daily pending laboratory confirmation of vitamin D deficiency and iron deficiency anemia. Avoid metformin, SGLT2 inhibitors, chronic NSAIDs, dual ACE‑I/ARB therapy, lithium, and unprotected IV contrast due to severe renal impairment. Obtain baseline labs, monitor renal function, electrolytes, lipids, and iron parameters, and review blood pressure and medication tolerability within 2 weeks.
